title: EIP-8250: Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions
description: Independent nonce domains for frame transactions
author: Thomas Thiery (@soispoke), Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation), lightclient (@lightclient), Vitalik Buterin (@vbuterin)
laymanDescription: A sender's transactions are processed in one strict order, so a single stuck transaction blocks every later one. Privacy protocols route many unrelated users through one shared sender, where that queue becomes a bottleneck. This proposal lets each transaction pick its own independent nonce sequence.
benefits: Unrelated users sharing a sender stop invalidating each other's pending transactions
Gives single-use keys an atomic spent-once guarantee that survives later frame reverts
Keyed state lives in a system contract, leaving the account trie layout untouched
tradeoffs: Each first-use key permanently occupies a storage slot, surcharged 20,000 gas
Nonce keys are visible in the payload, so the choice of key domain is not private
Cancelling by resending at the same legacy nonce no longer works for keyed transactions
